name: CleanYourTV
works_with: Android TV and Google TV; Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or Antigravity CLI to do it for you
short: Strips ads and bloatware from an Android or Google TV over Wi-Fi and gives it a clean Apple TV style home screen.
what: It uses the TV's own debug bridge over Wi-Fi to back up its settings, disable the maker's telemetry, ad services and preloaded apps, and install a small launcher as the new home screen. Nothing is rooted or uninstalled, so one restore command undoes it. You can let a coding assistant run it from the repo's prompt in about fifteen minutes, or run the scripts yourself.
who: Owners of an Android TV or Google TV who are tired of sponsored rows and are fine with a terminal. Samsung, LG, Roku, Vizio and Hisense VIDAA sets are not supported, and Fire TV gets the debloat only.
needs: An Android TV or Google TV on the same Wi-Fi as your computer
A JDK from 17 through 22 and Android SDK platform 34 with build-tools 34, to build the launcher
Optional: a coding assistant such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or Antigravity CLI

steps.title: Turn on debugging on the TV
steps.text: Settings, Device Preferences, About, then press OK on Build seven times. Go back to Developer options and turn USB debugging on. Turn on Network or ADB debugging too if you see it.

steps.title: Clone the repo
steps.text: Cloning matters: the assistant reuses the repo's scripts, which hold the backup and the restore record.

steps.title: Let your assistant do it
steps.text: Open the folder in your coding assistant, paste `PROMPT.md` and fill in your TV model. Accept "Allow USB debugging?" on the TV, then answer its checklist: which apps you use, the dock, and whether to keep the voice assistant, Chromecast and updates.

steps.title: Or set up the tools by hand
steps.code:
python3 -m venv tools/venv && tools/venv/bin/pip install -r tools/requirements.txt
export TV_HOST=192.168.1.50

steps.title: Apply a debloat list and install the launcher
steps.text: Use the list for your model from `examples/`. This example is for a Xiaomi Mi TV 4A.

steps.title: Restore if you change your mind
Close debugging when done
steps.text: In Developer options turn USB, Network and Wireless debugging off, revoke the authorisations, reboot, then check the port is closed.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Check what you're working with first: `tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py --probe` prints the TV's model, Android version and firmware.

watch: Network ADB is plaintext on port 5555, and on some firmware any device on your network gets a shell. Turn debugging off when you're done.
The risk is disabling something the TV relies on. If it won't start far enough to re-enable apps in Settings, a factory reset is usually the way back.
A firmware update brings the packages back and returns Home to the stock launcher. Run `tools/check.py` with `--fix` after one.
Changing a TV's software may affect its warranty or support. You run it at your own risk.
Only cleanyour.tv and this repo are official. Other sites using the name are not, and it has no app in any app store.
